explain.say: The Great Pyramid at Giza was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for nearly 4,000 years. It was built around 2560 BCE for King Khufu, more than 2,000 years before Cleopatra. Look at the timeline: ancient Egypt lasted so long that Cleopatra lived closer to us than to Khufu.

explain.say: Everything depended on the river. See the cycle. Each summer the Nile flooded, leaving rich black mud, so Egyptians called their land Kemet, the black land. Three seasons: flood, growing and harvest. The Greek historian Herodotus called Egypt the gift of the river. What happens to a farming kingdom when the flood fails?

stages.note: July to October, the Nile covers the fields.
stages.ask: Why was the Nile flood so important?

stages.label: Peret: growing
stages.note: Sow wheat and barley in black mud.

stages.label: Shemu: harvest
stages.note: Reap, thresh and pay grain tax.

explain.say: Now the Great Pyramid. Who built it? Not slaves in chains, as films once showed. Archaeologists found a workers' town at Giza with bakeries, breweries and tombs for workers who died. Crews of paid labourers, with farmers serving their turn, did the work. About 2.3 million stone blocks! How would you organise that?

explain.say: Jump to the New Kingdom, from about 1550 BCE. Look at the map. Pharaohs pushed south into Nubia, today's Sudan, and north into Syria. Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh for about twenty years. Ramesses II fought the Hittites at Kadesh, then signed one of the earliest surviving peace treaties. Why might two empires choose peace?

Old Kingdom kings were buried in pyramids; New Kingdom kings in hidden rock tombs in the Valley of the Kings, like Tutankhamun's, found in 1922. Superb work. Exam tip: when you compare kingdoms, compare power, tombs and foreign reach, and always give approximate dates.

faq.a: Paid Egyptian workers and farmers serving labour duty, organised in crews and fed by the state. Excavations of a workers' town and tombs at Giza show they were not slaves in the popular sense.
asks: How was the Great Pyramid built?

faq.a: The tomb of King Khufu of the Fourth Dynasty, built around 2560 BCE at Giza. It was originally about 146 metres tall and contains roughly 2.3 million stone blocks.
asks: How tall is the Great Pyramid?

faq.q: What was the difference between the Old and New Kingdom?
faq.a: The Old Kingdom, about 2686 to 2181 BCE, was the age of pyramid building within Egypt. The New Kingdom, about 1550 to 1069 BCE, was an imperial age with conquests in Nubia and the Levant and rock-cut royal tombs.

faq.q: Why was the Nile flood so important?
faq.a: The yearly flood watered the fields and laid down fertile silt, allowing big harvests in a desert land. Taxes, food stores and the whole calendar were organised around it.
asks: Why was the Nile important to Egypt?

faq.q: What was the treaty of Kadesh?
faq.a: A peace treaty between Ramesses II of Egypt and the Hittite king Hattusili III, made around 1259 BCE, years after the Battle of Kadesh. Copies survive in Egyptian hieroglyphs and in Akkadian on clay tablets.
asks: What was the first peace treaty?

facts: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was built around 2560 BCE and stood about 146 metres tall.
Hatshepsut ruled Egypt as pharaoh for about 20 years in the fifteenth century BCE.
Howard Carter found Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings in 1922.
